sources.publisher: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes the live, country-by-country ordinary-passport visa regime on its official mfa.gov.tr domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Ordinary passport holders are exempted from visa up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

sources.title: Law on Foreigners and International Protection, Law No. 6458
sources.publisher: Presidency of Migration Management, Ministry of Interior
sources.officialityEvidence: The Presidency of Migration Management hosts the English text of Law No. 6458 on its official goc.gov.tr domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Foreigners wishing to stay in Turkey for up to ninety days shall obtain a visa that indicates the purpose of their visit.

sources.title: Passport Law No. 5682
sources.publisher: General Directorate of Population and Citizenship Affairs, Ministry of Interior
sources.officialityEvidence: The Interior Ministry's population and citizenship directorate publishes the English Passport Law on its official nvi.gov.tr domain.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Those who arrive at the borders of Türkiye and claim Turkish citizenship shall be admitted to Türkiye.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: short visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry's current country schedule expressly exempts these ordinary passports for the stated short tourist, business, transit, or general-visit period.
conditions: The Ministry gives country-specific periods: most are 90 days in 180 days, while Belarus, Brunei, Costa Rica, Indonesia, Mongolia, Russia, Thailand, Venezuela, and Macao have expressly different limits. China is expressly effective from 2026-01-02.

Where the schedule says tourism, business, transit, or tourist purpose, that stated purpose limitation remains. Work, study, residence, documentary filming, research, excavation, truck-driver, crew, diplomatic, official, and special-document regimes are not flattened into this policy.

The Law's general maximum is 90 days in 180 days unless the applicable exemption states otherwise. A passport or travel document normally must remain valid 60 days beyond the authorised stay, and a visa exemption does not remove admissibility or entry-ban checks.

policies.title: Antigua and Barbuda, Dominican Republic, and Saint Vincent: visa obtainable at entry
policies.summary: The Foreign Ministry expressly permits these ordinary passport holders to obtain a visa at Turkish ports of entry; the easier arrival-issued route controls over their parallel e-Visa option.
conditions: The current Ministry schedule says Antigua and Barbuda, the Dominican Republic, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines may obtain three-month multiple-entry visas at ports of entry, as well as by e-Visa or Turkish missions.

This policy is a genuine border-issued visa, not an inference from an online form. Article 13 permits border visas only in exceptional cases and subjects them to applicable documents, insurance, funds, purpose, admissibility, and border-officer requirements.
Work, study, residence, official, service, diplomatic, crew, and special-travel-document rules are outside this ordinary short-visitor policy.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance visa required baseline
policies.summary: For these ordinary passports, the current Foreign Ministry schedule expressly says a visa is required and does not itself establish a reproducible ordinary-passport e-Visa or arrival-visa route.
conditions: This is the current ordinary-passport baseline from the Ministry's country-by-country schedule. The Law normally directs a foreigner without a visa exemption to obtain the purpose-specific visa at a Turkish consulate in the citizenship or legal-residence country.

It does not erase country-specific diplomatic, official, service, special, crew, residence, work, study, transit, or other exceptional arrangements. Visas do not confer an absolute right of entry and remain subject to statutory document, insurance, funds, security, health, purpose, and entry-ban controls.

policies.title: Turkish ordinary passport: citizen admission
policies.summary: A person claiming Turkish citizenship is statutorily admitted at Türkiye's border once the prescribed citizenship evidence is established.
conditions: Passport Law No. 5682 requires normal passport or valid substitute-document presentation at entry and specifies admission even where a claimant arrives without one once Turkish citizenship is proved.
This is a citizen-entry rule, not a foreign visitor visa or passport-waiver classification.

unresolved.reason: The MFA splits Algerian ordinary passports by age: under 15 and over 50 are visa-exempt, 15-18 and 35-50 may have a conditional e-Visa, and the remaining age range requires a visa. A passport-only status is not established.

The MFA makes Iraqi ordinary-passport treatment age- and document-dependent: under 15 and over 50 are visa-exempt; ages 15-50 need a visa but may have a conditional e-Visa. A passport-only status is not established.

The MFA splits Libyan ordinary-passport treatment by age: under 16 and over 45 are visa-exempt, while ages 16-45 require a visa and may have a conditional e-Visa. A passport-only status is not established.
